title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of a typed letter from Grothendieck to Deligne dated 10.12.1965. It sits among papers on crystals and de Rham cohomology, but this first part concerns étale Poincaré duality, i.e. the material that became SGA 4 Exposé XVIII ('La formule de dualité globale', written by Deligne).

Setting: f: X → Y is smooth, compactifiable, of relative dimension d. A is a torsion coefficient ring (n invertible on Y). The claim to prove is that the trace map Rf_! f^*(d)[2d] → id makes f^! ≅ f^*(d)[2d] a right adjoint of Rf_!. Equivalently, for all F and G the map Rf_* RHom(F, f^*G(d)[2d]) → RHom(Rf_!F, G) is an isomorphism.

Part 1 (simplification). Earlier dévissages (fibering into curves, reducing F to A_X and G to A_Y) had reduced the problem to relative dimension 1 with F = A_X and G = A_Y. Grothendieck proposes avoiding the relative purity theorem as follows:
(i) Use the limit argument of SGA 4 VI §6 to make Y noetherian, indeed of finite type over Z, hence finite-dimensional.
(ii) Induct on dimension. The text says n = dim X; the effective induction is on the dimension of the base.
(iii) Localize to Y strictly local with closed point y. Then dim(Y−y) < n, so the open part X ×_Y (Y−y) is covered by induction. The closed fibre X ×_Y y lies over a strictly henselian base of dimension 0, essentially the curve-over-a-separably-closed-field case, which is known.
(iv) 'On gagne.'

Why one can treat the two pieces separately. For general G, use the triangle G → Rj_*j^*G → (cone supported at y). Smooth base change gives f^! Rj_* = Rj'_* f'^!. Proper base change gives compatibility of i_* with Rf_! for the closed point. So duality for G of the form Rj_*G' or i_*G'' reduces to duality over Y−y and over y.

Part 2 (generalization). Duality holds with the same statement for smooth compactifiable f between ringed topoi f: (X,B) → (Y,A), where:
- A is any sheaf of rings on Y killed by an integer n prime to the residue characteristics;
- B is any sheaf of rings on X with a ring map f^{-1}A → B.
One defines f^!(K) = RHom_{f^{-1}A}(B, f^{-1}K ⊗ T_{X/Y}[2d]), with T the Tate/orientation twist (d). Trace and duality factor through (X, f^{-1}A) → (Y,A), handled like A = Z/n, and the change of rings (X,B) → (X, f^{-1}A), which is trivial: it is the coinduction adjunction. Grothendieck suggests including this general form in SGA 4. He doubts it follows formally from the Z/n case. The next page says the same holds for global duality, and then turns to the p-adic comparison conjecture.
errors: The text says the induction is on n = dim X, but the dimension drop used is dim(Y−y) < dim Y. The induction must really be on dim Y (for relative dimension 1, dim X = dim Y + 1, so the two are equivalent up to a shift).

'On est réduit à prouver le théorème séparément pour X×_Y(Y−y) et X×_Y y' is stated without justification. With the fixed G = A_Y, the stalk of RHom(Rf_!A_X, A_Y) at y is not a fibre computation. Splitting into open and closed parts naively brings in i^!A_Y, which is exactly a purity-type input.
- The reduction works if one returns to general G and uses smooth base change for Rj_* together with proper base change.
- The letter does not spell this out, so 'on gagne' hides a small gap.
The closed fibre over a strictly local base is the curve-over-separably-closed-field case, not literally 'n = 0'. The base case is mislabelled but the content is standard.

ideas.what: Proof of smooth étale Poincaré duality avoiding relative purity, by noetherian/finite-type approximation, localization to strictly local bases, and induction on the base dimension via the open/closed decomposition Y−y ∪ y.
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré–Verdier duality for smooth morphisms in étale cohomology (f^! = f^*(d)[2d]) via dévissage on the base
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier; written up by Deligne in SGA 4 XVIII (1965–73)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. XVIII (Deligne); unsure whether this exact induction is the argument printed there

ideas.what: Duality for a smooth compactifiable morphism of ringed étale topoi (X,B) → (Y,A) with A any n-torsion ring sheaf and B arbitrary, using f^!K = RHom_{f^{-1}A}(B, f^{-1}K ⊗ T[2d]); proof splits into the case f^{-1}A = B and the pure change-of-rings case.
ideas.modern_name: Coinduction / exceptional pullback for morphisms of ringed topoi; duality with general torsion coefficient ring sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, SGA 4 XVIII (which works with fairly general torsion coefficient rings); change-of-rings right adjoint is folklore
ideas.where_published: Possibly absorbed into SGA 4 XVIII (unsure of the exact generality printed)

ideas.what: Suggestion that global duality also holds for ring sheaves more general than constant Z/n (continued on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Duality with coefficients in sheaves of rings

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal SGA 4 editorial correspondence: a proof simplification and a natural generalization of duality to ringed topoi, both of which flowed into or are routine relative to Deligne's Exposé XVIII. It is historically nice as a document of Grothendieck shaping XVIII, but not mathematically new. The genuinely striking part of the letter is the p-adic comparison speculation on the next page, which anticipates p-adic Hodge theory.
transcription_corrections: 'f:X  Y' should read 'f:X → Y' (arrows dropped throughout).
'si on y tien' should read 'si on y tient'.
In the formula, 'f^{-1}(K)⊗T_{X/Y} 2d)' should read 'f^{-1}(K) ⊗ T_{X/Y}[2d]': the bracket shift [2d] was dropped, and T_{X/Y} is the Tate twist/orientation sheaf.
